newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine-Russia sugar tax dispute continues-agency.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine-Russia sugar tax dispute continues-agency.

text.p: A dispute over a 25 percent Russian duty on imports of Ukrainian sugar is far from settled, Interfax-Ukraine news agency quoted the head of the National Association of Ukrainian Sugar Producers as saying on Thursday.

Ukraine had been hopeful Russia would remove the tax, implemented in May after Russia accused Ukraine of dumping cheap sugar on its markets, following talks during President Boris Yeltsin's visit to Kiev at the end of May.
"There is a complicated situation with Russia. Ukraine wants Russia to remove the tax, but Russia thinks it's right," Ihor Rylyk said. "We're at a dead end."
Rylyk said Ukrainian sugar would not sell for such high prices in Russia, a traditional buyer of Ukrainian sugar.
He added wholesale sugar prices were $600 per tonne in Ukraine but was selling in Russia for $370-400 per tonne.
